summary: Yakima County DNR 40-foot wooden tower built 1961 on Pine Mountain; standing in 2006, gone by 2012; no source found describes what, if anything, remains on the site.

facts.status_note: Still standing in 2006 and gone by 2012; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the site

access.note: Willhite reports the property was owned by Pine Mountain LLC in 2015; an undated National Geodetic Survey station description on Forest Lookouts (recovery notes 1966 and 1971) says to obtain a key to a locked gate. Private status is inferred from the LLC owner, not a posted rule

events.note: A Metsker map labels the high point of Cowiche Mountain as Cowiche L.O. Willhite reads this as a possible earlier lookout; not confirmed by any source

DNR tower built; the register and firelookout.com say it is the only lookout structure ever on the site. Forest Lookouts quotes a state biennial report saying the DNR carpentry crew finished nine lookouts at about $8,000 each, one at Pine Mountain
Gone by 2012; the removal date is not given
Registered August 15, 2012 as US 1377, WA 277; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say the 1961 tower is the only lookout structure ever on the site. Willhite cites 1934 and 1959 Metsker maps that label a Cowiche L.O. at the high point, but calls an earlier lookout a gut feeling. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: No staffing or fire records in these sources. A Yakima Herald piece on Mike Hiler's book about Yakima County lookouts returned HTTP 429 and was not read; it may add local detail. The NGS station description on Forest Lookouts is undated, but its recovery notes date from 1966 and 1971, so its access directions may be old. Brief status gone is consistent with the sources. Willhite's Cowiche Lookout claim is unconfirmed and is reported as a conflict, not as fact.
